en: Itivuttaka 64: Tikanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard: “Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a stone pillar, the person who is like a tree stump, and the person who is like a lotus. And how, monks, is one a person like a stone pillar? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hate, harboring ill will toward beings. Just as a stone pillar, though struck by rain and wind, remains unshaken and unmoved; even so, monks, that person dwells with a mind full of hate, harboring ill will toward beings. This, monks, is called a person like a stone pillar. And how, monks, is one a person like a tree stump? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hate, harboring ill will toward beings. Just as a tree stump, though struck by rain and wind, remains unshaken and unmoved; even so, monks, that person dwells with a mind full of hate, harboring ill will toward beings. This, monks, is called a person like a tree stump. And how, monks, is one a person like a lotus? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind free from hate, without ill will toward beings. Just as a lotus, though struck by rain and wind, remains unshaken and unmoved; even so, monks, that person dwells with a mind free from hate, without ill will toward beings. This, monks, is called a person like a lotus. These, monks, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, a certain monk approached the Venerable Ānanda and said to him: “Friend Ānanda, what is the meaning of this that was said by the Blessed One: ‘There are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world’? “It is wonderful, friend, it is marvelous, friend! How well has the meaning of this been explained by the Venerable Ānanda, just as it was explained by the Blessed One himself when he taught the Dhamma to the disciples in brief, and how the Venerable Ānanda now explains its detailed meaning. [The Venerable Ānanda then repeated the entire discourse to the monk. “Indeed, friend, it is wonderful, it is marvelous! How well has the meaning of this been explained by the Venerable Ānanda, just as it was explained by the Blessed One himself when he taught the Dhamma to the disciples in brief, and how the Venerable Ānanda now explains its detailed meaning. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. "Monks, there are these three kinds of misconduct."
Misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, and misconduct of mind—
these, monks, are the three kinds of misconduct.”
